item.title: Rubio says US and Europe belong together after Greenland dispute
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that the United States wants a strong Europe and aims to rebuild the transatlantic alliance after recent disputes, including tensions over Greenland. item.title: Foreign workers have lower crime rates than Danes, new study finds
item.description: New analysis finds employment, not origin, determines crime rates, with foreign workers committing fewer offenses than Danish citizens overall.

item.title: We don’t really talk about failure,” but “failure is part of the process.” How Roxy transformed failure into a popular event series
item.description: Roxy, a 33-year-old Romanian entrepreneur, founded an event series to challenge how failure is viewed. “There’s a relatively big amount of shame that comes with failure,” she says. “You don’t want to look stupid. You don’t want to say to your family and friends that you failed.”

item.title: 2 in 3 parents financially support adult children
item.description: A YouGov survey for Nordea reveals that two out of three parents provide financial support to their adult children aged 18 to 29. item.title: Jacob Mark named SF lead candidate in Hillerød
item.description: Prominent SF politician Jacob Mark is returning to the political arena as the party’s lead candidate in Hillerød for the upcoming general election. Mark previously withdrew from politics after suffering stress-related vision loss. item.title: Løkke opens Rwanda embassy after new Africa strategy
item.description: Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen travels to Rwanda on Sunday to open Denmark’s new embassy, reflecting the government’s ambition to strengthen its presence in Africa with “less moralism and more equality.” Part of a broader strategy including new embassies in Senegal and Tunisia, the move comes amid concerns over China’s influence. item.title: Venstre to cut billions from development aid
item.description: Venstre’s chairman, Troels Lund Poulsen, proposes lowering Denmark’s development aid from 0.7% to 0.5% of Gross National Income (GNI). This change would free up approximately 6.5 billion DKK to be reinvested in welfare and security. item.title: Police warn of drifting snow Monday morning
item.description: On the first day following the school winter holidays, Danish police urge caution in Monday morning traffic due to drifting snow. East Jutland Police report challenges in Aarhus Municipality, where large snow piles have accumulated on main and side roads. item.title: Prison choir to live on after leader’s death
item.description: The Prison Choir, composed of current and former Danish inmates, will continue under “Danmarks Fængsler” (Danish Prisons), which was not previously part of the project.
